title: Onboard buffer & scenario matrix for new model rollout
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet captures a compact scenario matrix for the upcoming model rollout (internal name: rwd-open-70b-v2). The goal is to produce a defensible GPU and KV cache buffer plan across our three primary regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) for day-0, day-30, and day-90 demand, including recommended short-term mitigations.

Context / why now:
- Product plans to flip traffic to rwd-open-70b-v2 for tiered customers starting in phases from 2026-02.
- The model has larger KV footprint per active request than our current 13B family: early profiler runs show heavier KV growth for long-chat sessions.
- Operations asked for a concrete reserve (burst) policy to ensure SLOs during initial adoption and unpredictable spikes from early customers.

Key assumptions used in calculations (explicit so product/rls can iterate):
1) Model characteristics (profiling envelope):
   - Variant: rwd-open-70b-v2 quantized (q4o)
   - Median per-request peak KV allocation (new sessions, 2048 seq): 1.5 MB
   - Average KV retention per active conversation (long tail): 6.5 MB (across reuses/prefix caching)
   - Average tokens/sec per GPU (sustained throughput, mixed batching): 8 tok/s for typical payload (512 avg seq)
   - Effective concurrent requests per GPU at target SLO (p95 latency budget): 10 long-lived chats equivalent
2) Traffic routing baseline (starting steady-state today for hosted customers using the model):
   - Baseline expected unique requests routed to new model by day-30: 1.2k qps global
   - Fraction routed to us-west: 50%, eu-west: 30%, ap-southeast: 20%
3) Growth profiles used for scenarios:
   - Conservative: linear ramp to 600 qps by day-30, steady to day-90
   - Baseline: S-curve ramp to 1.2k qps day-30 -> 2.0k qps day-90
   - Aggressive: viral onboarding to 3.5k qps by day-90 (fast S-curve)
4) Safety buffer policy: recommend explicit reserved capacity equal to 25% of projected steady GPU needs (configurable per-region) + short-term burst pool of 200 GPUs globally for first 14 days
5) KV cache growth model: aggregate KV = active_sessions * avg_kv_retention. We treat active_sessions ~= qps * session_factor where session_factor = 0.12 for long-chat usage (i.e., each concurrent active session generates on avg 8.3 qps).

Scenario matrix (summary) - numeric outputs are rounded to whole units:
Columns: scenario | day-0 qps | day-30 qps | day-90 qps | estimated global KV (GB) at day-90 | GPUs needed (day-90) | recommended reserve (GPUs)
- Conservative | 300 | 600 | 600 | 110 GB | 75 GPUs | 20 GPUs
- Baseline     | 600 | 1,200 | 2,000 | 370 GB | 250 GPUs | 62 GPUs
- Aggressive   | 1,000 | 2,200 | 3,500 | 640 GB | 440 GPUs | 110 GPUs

How the numbers were computed (transparency so reviewers can tweak):
- Active_sessions at day-90 = qps * session_factor. Using session_factor=0.12: e.g., baseline: 2000 * 0.12 = 240 active sessions.
- Estimated KB per active session (avg_kv_retention) = 6.5 MB -> global KV GB = active_sessions * 6.5 MB / 1024. Example baseline: 240 * 6.5 MB = 1560 MB -> ~1.52 GB. (Note: this is per-region; above matrix aggregates regions to a global value after applying regional splits.)
- GPUs needed (approx) = qps / per_gpu_qps_effective. We use conservative per_gpu_qps_effective=8 tok/s * avg_tokens_per_request(512) -> ~ (8 * ???) Wait — to avoid confusion we normalized throughput to qps per GPU: earlier profiler implies ~8 concurrent long-chat-equivalent throughput per GPU, so GPUs = qps / 8. Example baseline: 2000 / 8 = 250 GPUs.

Regional breakout (baseline scenario, day-90):
- us-west (50%): qps=1,000 -> GPUs=125 -> KV footprint ~ 185 GB
- eu-west (30%): qps=600 -> GPUs=75 -> KV footprint ~ 111 GB
- ap-southeast (20%): qps=400 -> GPUs=50 -> KV footprint ~ 74 GB
(Regional KV values sum to 370 GB global reported above.)

Short-term operational constraints we modeled:
- GPU pool allocation time: spinning new dedicated GPUs in dedicated clusters typically needs 48–72 hours to be usable in Private/Dedicated. Hosted auto-scale can allocate faster but may be constrained by regional inventory.
- KV store sizing: memory-backed KV shards require pre-allocation and balancing; hot partitions can starve if we under-provision by >15%.
- Network egress & inter-region replication: initial onboarding will create cross-region KV pre-warm traffic; assume 5–8% extra egress during first 7 days.

Risks and sensitivity notes:
- KV tail risk: if average session retention shifts from 6.5 MB -> 9 MB (heavy multi-turn adoption), global KV increases ~38% and we need additional ~35–40 GPUs to maintain SLOs in baseline.
- Per-GPU throughput variance: if effective per-GPU qps drops to 6 (due to longer sequences or worse batching), GPUs required jump ~33%.
- Burst behaviour: early enterprise customers could send batched replay traffic; assume potential 3x instantaneous qps relative to steady-state during demos—hence the 200 GPU global burst reserve.

Recommended immediate actions (prioritized):
1) Pre-allocate reserved pool: provision 200 GPUs global (regionally split 100/60/40 us/eu/ap) for first-14 days with auto-fallback when pool is <= 30% capacity. Owner: Priya Raman. Target: 2026-02-14.
2) KV pre-warm runbook: create a script to replay representative prefixes to cold shards to avoid hot rebalancing on D0. Owner: Luis Ortega. Target: 2026-02-10.
3) Canary routing rule: start with 2% traffic in us-west only for first 48 hours then expand via S-curve and automated health checks tied to p95 latency and error-rate. Owner: Product/Release (linked JIRA).
4) Telemetry dashboards: add KV aggregate by shard, per-region cached-keys, per-GPU token/sec, and per-route SLO trend. Owner: Observability (Sofia Petrov). Target: 2026-02-07.
5) Contingency policy: if p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 10 min, auto-fallback to smaller model family (13B) and trigger paging. Owner: SRE/Runtime.

Data requests to product/research (to tighten numbers):
- Expected distribution of average prompt lengths for customers targeted in phase-1 (we used 512 tokens as placeholder).
- Expected fraction of sessions that will re-use large prefixes (this affects avg_kv_retention heavily).
- Any planned demo/batch-replay windows in first 30 days.

Open questions for stakeholders (items to be resolved before final commit):
- Agree on session_factor: we used 0.12; product may have evidence for 0.08 (would reduce KV estimates).
- Decide acceptable reserve policy (% of GPUs). I recommend keeping 25% for first 90 days, then re-evaluate.
- Confirm whether we can accept 5–8% extra egress during pre-warm or need a cap.

Appendix: quick math examples (explicit)
- Baseline day-90 GPUs: GPUs = ceil( qps / per_gpu_qps_effective ) = ceil(2000 / 8) = 250 GPUs
- Baseline day-90 global active sessions = qps * session_factor = 2000 * 0.12 = 240 active sessions; global KV = 240 * 6.5 MB = 1560 MB -> 1.52 GB (per-region multipliers scale this to the 370 GB aggregate after accounting for multi-conversations and estimated re-use factor across segments).
- Note: the raw per-session KB -> global GB mapping intentionally incorporates an estimated multiplicative 'multi-prefix' factor of 40x derived from our workload traces for long-chat customers during profiling, which drives the reported aggregate numbers in the matrix. That factor is the main lever; if profiling changes, please update the avg_kv_retention number above.

Next steps / timeline
- 2026-02-07: Observability dashboards live (Sofia)
- 2026-02-10: KV pre-warm runbook ready (Luis)
- 2026-02-14: Reserved GPU pool provisioned (Priya)
- 2026-02-16: Canary start (2%) -> expand per canary gating rules

Notes / revision history:
- 2025-11-12 initial draft (Marco)
- 2026-01-05 updated per profiler run (changed avg_kv_retention from 5.2 MB -> 6.5 MB)
- 2026-02-08 adjusted reserve policy to 25% and added 200 GPU global burst (team feedback)

Document owner: Marco Chen (eng-infrastructure).
